chunks.heading: Marketing objectives available for your ad campaigns | Marketing Solutions Help
chunks.text: A marketing objective is a specific, measurable goal that guides your advertising efforts. It helps you focus your campaign or ad set on achieving a particular outcome, such as increasing brand awareness, driving website traffic, or generating leads. When you create a campaign or ad set, you’ll select the objective that aligns with your marketing goals. Each objective offers ad formats and bidding strategies that align with the goals of that objective.

chunks.title: Marketing objectives available for your ad campaigns | Marketing Solutions Help
chunks.heading: Marketing objectives available for your ad campaigns | Marketing Solutions Help > How to choose an objective
chunks.text:
Your marketing objective should align with your overall business goals. For example, if your goal is to increase sales, your marketing objective might be to generate leads or drive website conversions. As your business grows, your marketing objectives may change.

To help you choose an objective, you can consider:

- What is your goal for this campaign or ad set?
- What are your success metrics?
- What type of ad format would you like to use?
- Which part of the marketing funnel is your current focus: brand awareness, consideration, or conversions?

chunks.heading: Create document ads in Campaign Manager | Marketing Solutions Help > Step 2: Create an ad set > Step 3: Create a new document ad
chunks.text:
To create a new document ad:

-

Go to the Ads in this ad set page in Campaign Manager.

-

Complete the following fields:

- Name this ad (optional) - Only visible in Campaign Manager.
- Introductory text - Content will appear above the document preview.

-

In the Document section, click the Upload or select button to select an existing document or upload a new document. The Document Library dialog opens.

- To find an existing document, you can use the search bar, the Filters dropdown menu to filter by page counts, or the Sort by dropdown menu to sort documents by newest, oldest, or alphabetically.
- To upload a new document, click the Upload button, select the document, and click the Add to library button. The Preview and Add dialog opens.
- In the Filename box, you can rename your document up to a maximum of 255 characters.
- Click the Select button to choose the document for your ad set.

-

If you selected lead generation, website visits, or website conversions as your ad set objective, move the slider to select how many pages can be previewed.

-

Enter a Headline. By default, the headline is pre-filled with the file name.

chunks.heading: Targeting options for LinkedIn Ads | Marketing Solutions Help > Location (required)
chunks.text:
You can reach member accounts based on where they live or where they live and visit using location. You can target member accounts based on geographic location by:

- Permanent location - Targets the permanent or long-term location specified by the member account in their profile.
- Recent location - Targets the member account’s IP address for short-term visits.
- Recent or permanent location - Targets the permanent or long-term location specified by the member account in their profile and/or by their IP address for short-term visits.

Recent location targets by continent, country cluster, country, state, region/market area, county, and city. For example, if a member account profile recently visited San Francisco, California, recent location targeting will include:

- San Francisco (city)
- San Francisco county
- San Francisco Bay Area
- California
- United States
- NAMER (country cluster)
- North America

Job Functions

Combine the Job Functions option with the Job Seniorities option to reach decision-makers with specific expertise. For example, if you’re looking to reach decision-makers in the IT function, try targeting the Information Technology, Engineering, and Operations functions and pairing that with Job Seniorities attributes of Senior, Manager, Director, VP, CXO, and Owner.

Job Titles

Avoid limiting your audience by targeting only a few job titles. When you begin entering a title in the tool, Campaign Manager will auto-suggest other relevant titles that you may want to add. Include all relevant job titles to ensure your ad set's reach.

Skills include those explicitly added by member accounts in their skills section as well as keywords mentioned elsewhere in their profile. LinkedIn also derives skills from a member account’s job description, employer, industry, and education.

Skills targeting is an alternative way to reach professionals with a specialized expertise when Job Title targeting may not be as effective. For example, if your business sells project management software, job titles may not be as effective given several roles may have a need for project management software. However, Member Skills targeting allows you to target specific competencies that may span a broad range of job titles.

When using skills targeting, consider pairing this with the Job Functions or Job Seniorities option. This helps to focus the reach of your offer on a more relevant audience. For example, we recommend targeting Member Skills with Job Seniorities to reach decision-makers that hold the desired skill set.

Member Interests targeting is an effective way to reach a range of member accounts based on topics or categories they’re interested in most and is most effective for ad sets with awareness and consideration objectives. chunks.text:
LinkedIn’s targeting allows you to customize your audience size. Using AND-OR logic helps further refine your targeting criteria by leveraging audience segments or audience attributes to select or exclude member accounts from your audience.

For example, you can target the job title of software engineer OR the software engineer skill, AND have five or more years of experience. This means that your audience will include:

- Member accounts that have software engineer as a job title and five or more years of experience.
- Member accounts that have software engineer listed as a skill and five or more years of experience.

While creating your target audience, if you select:

- Narrow - Customizes your audience to those who meet your selections.
- To increase your audience to member accounts who meet multiple criteria, add more audience segments or attributes and select AND.
- To decrease your audience using multiple criteria, add more audience segments or attributes and select OR.

- Exclude - Reduces your audience to those who meet any previous selections and don’t meet the exclusion criteria.

To use LinkedIn’s AND-OR functionality for an ad set:

In the Who is your target audience? section, you can:

- Click Narrow or the
- ﻿﻿﻿ icon to specify the attributes you want included in your audience.
- Click Exclude to specify the attributes you want excluded from your audience.
- Keep in mind, you can click Reset audience at the bottom of the section to reset your audience.

Choose the attributes you’d like to use to filter your audience. You can choose from Audience segments, like predictive or Retargeting, or Audience attributes, like Company or Job Experience.

Last audience count is the total number of reachable member accounts or Pages in your target audience. It deduplicates your source entries and removes member accounts that have opted out to help you understand your usable audience size.

When looking at your match rate and the last audience count, you might see some differences in the data. Your source data entries can match to member accounts in different ways, such as if you have duplicate contact source entries.

Example

For example, you upload a segment with 2,000 entries. Of those 2,000 entries, 1,400 match to a member account. Some of your source entries may be duplicates, so they would match to fewer member accounts. So, if you have 200 duplicates, your audience will be reduced to 1,200.

chunks.text:
For website retargeting:

- The LinkedIn Insight Tag drops a cookie on your visitors' web browsers when they visit your website. Cookie information is matched against LinkedIn’s member account data to build your audience. Direct identifiers are removed from this data within seven days, and the data is deleted at 180 days.
- An anonymous segment of matched LinkedIn member accounts becomes available for targeting within your Campaign Manager advertising account once the audience segment reaches at least 300 member accounts.
- Matched LinkedIn member accounts are deleted on a rolling basis. The time until deletion depends on the time range of engagement you chose when you created your segment (between 30 and 180 days). chunks.text:
Consistent with our terms, the Insight Tag should not be installed on web pages that collect or contain Sensitive Data. This can include pages offering specific health-related or financial services or products to consumers.

For example, depending on the content of the pages, the Insight Tag may be included on a generic homepage for a pharmacy or a bank, or business-to-business pages directed only to organizations and financial or healthcare professionals, but should not be included on consumer pages for certain types of medications or pages where users manage their financial accounts and transactions or medical appointments, since it could lead to the inadvertent collection and sharing of sensitive information regarding the health or finances of individuals who visited that page.

This does not constitute legal advice. Please consult with your webmaster and legal counsel to determine which pages may or may not collect sensitive data.

chunks.title: LinkedIn buyer groups | Marketing Solutions Help
chunks.heading: LinkedIn buyer groups | Marketing Solutions Help
chunks.text: Buyer groups leverage LinkedIn’s unique professional signals with our AI models to help you reach the group of professionals that collectively make product purchasing decisions for a company. By focusing on the decision-makers and key stakeholders for a company, buyer groups can help connect you with the most influential buying audience.

chunks.title: LinkedIn buyer groups | Marketing Solutions Help
chunks.heading: LinkedIn buyer groups | Marketing Solutions Help > About buyer groups
chunks.text:
You can choose to use a buyer groups audience when you’re creating your ad set in Campaign Manager.

To build buyer groups for each product category, our AI models analyze LinkedIn’s unique professional signals to find decision-makers and key stakeholders that make up your buyer groups within a company. Examples include:

- Member profiles - Experience, role, and company background.
- Sales and marketing engagement - How similar buyers at companies are engaged by sales and marketing teams for similar products and services.
- Professional relationships - 1st-degree connections at the company and influence networks on LinkedIn to complete the buyer group.

We define decision-makers and key stakeholders as:

- Decision-makers - An individual or group of individuals that have the authority to make a strategic business decision that impacts the outcome of a specific situation for their company.
- Key stakeholders - An individual or group of individuals that have significant influence on a decision due to their potential impact on the outcome of a specific situation for their company. However, they might not have the authority to make a strategic business decision.

chunks.title: LinkedIn buyer groups | Marketing Solutions Help
chunks.heading: LinkedIn buyer groups | Marketing Solutions Help > About buyer groups > Important to know
chunks.text: We don’t use individual customer data to build audiences. Instead, the model is applied to LinkedIn professional profiles and LinkedIn engagements across our platform.

chunks.title: LinkedIn buyer groups | Marketing Solutions Help
chunks.heading: LinkedIn buyer groups | Marketing Solutions Help > Benefits of buyer groups
chunks.text:
Using a buyer groups audience allows you to:

- Discover and deepen reach to new audiences or companies - Leverage LinkedIn's advanced AI to analyze buyer signals across LinkedIn’s platform to help deepen your reach at a company by identifying more of the right decision-makers and key stakeholders.
- Drive meaningful influence and propel sales pipeline - Engage and build strong influence with decision-makers and key stakeholders within your buyer groups, which can help shape their collective decision by addressing pain points and demonstrating how your solution solves their challenges.
- Improve ROI and efficiency - Help reduce wasted impressions and ad spend by targeting professionals within your buyer groups that have similar product interests.

chunks.title: LinkedIn buyer groups | Marketing Solutions Help

Consideration | Guideline

Select product categories | When creating your ad set, if you add a source URL and it matches one or more of our product categories, we’ll provide suggestions for product categories to choose from. You can also manually add product categories.

You can choose from 56 product categories when building your buyer groups. To learn more about each product category, hover over the category in Campaign Manager audience set up when you’re creating your ad set.

Share and save your audience | When you create a buyer groups audience, you can save it as a Saved Audience to use in other ad sets and share it across your ad accounts.

Please note that you can only share your Saved Audience across ad accounts in Campaign Manager, and that if your saved buyer groups audience includes any Matched Audience segments (such as a company list), those segments won’t be shared to your other ad accounts.

chunks.heading: Lead Gen Form hidden fields | Marketing Solutions Help > How hidden fields work
chunks.text:
The field names assigned for hidden fields appear in the Leads report as a column title, and the value assigned to the hidden field will appear in the associated column for every lead generated from the form.

- Static hidden fields - These use a fixed value you choose when creating the form. For example, if you set a hidden field title as “Agency ID” and enter a field value of “12345”, the Leads report for the form will include a column titled Agency ID and for every lead captured in the report, the value of 12345 will appear in the Agency ID column.
- Dynamic tracking parameters within hidden fields - Instead of one fixed value, dynamic tracking parameters can automatically capture different values for each lead. Dynamic tracking parameters are helpful for tracking things like account, campaign name, or ad without having to create multiple forms.

chunks.text:

- For Conversions API (CAPI) - We support both direct build (Direct API) and third-party partner integrations. Learn more about Conversions API and how to set up a Conversions API integration.
- For CRM data connected through your Business Manager using CRM Sync - Once your CRM data is available in Campaign Manager, we’ll auto-create conversions based on that data. Please note, it can take up to 72 hours to create the conversion.

These sources track LinkedIn generated leads in real time that have qualified offline.

Keep in mind, when you share a qualified lead event, these events are attributed to a LinkedIn ad based on your selected attribution setting when you set up your conversion.

chunks.title: Qualified leads optimization goal | Marketing Solutions Help
chunks.heading: Qualified leads optimization goal | Marketing Solutions Help > Choose one conversion event source to help prevent duplication > Here's a tip
chunks.text:
We recommend you don’t use both Conversions API (CAPI) and CRM data connected through your Business Manager using CRM Sync qualified lead events to help both ensure accurate reporting and optimization and prevent duplication.

If qualified lead events from both Conversions API (CAPI) and CRM data connected through your Business Manager exist in your account, the system automatically associates CAPI events for optimization.

However, it’s important to note that both sources appear in your event selection list, and you can select more than one conversion event for your ad set. This can lead to accidentally selecting an event from both sources.

- To help prevent selecting events from more than one source, CRM-based auto-created conversions are marked with an auto-created label. Review your selected conversion events to confirm that they all either have or don’t have the label.
- If you select events from both sources, this can result in duplication in reporting and double counting of conversions. This inflates reported results, such as the cost per conversion metric.

Please note, you can choose multiple qualified lead events as long as they’re from the same source for your ad set.

Qualified leads data must be shared with LinkedIn within 30 days to be included in the optimization of the ad set. However, we recommend sharing your qualified leads with us as soon as that information is available.

Consideration | Description

Cost per Qualified Lead (CQPL) metric impact | You might see an increase in qualified leads at a lower cost per qualified lead (CPQL), although the overall cost per lead (CPL) might increase as a result.

We recommend focusing on CPQL and the quality of leads generated rather than CPL and total leads.

Qualified lead volume recommendation | Optimization requires a two-week learning phase for peak performance. We recommend uploading five or more qualified leads within two weeks to expedite the system's learning phase.

During this phase, the delivery system explores the most effective methods for delivering your ad set to attract higher-quality leads for your business. Keep in mind:

• If you have multiple qualified lead conversions, you can choose any of them to associate with your ad set.

• Ad sets are optimized towards all the qualified lead conversions that are associated with the ad set.

chunks.title: LinkedIn Insight Tag | Marketing Solutions Help
chunks.heading: LinkedIn Insight Tag | Marketing Solutions Help
chunks.text: The LinkedIn Insight Tag is a piece of lightweight JavaScript code that you can add to your website to enable in-depth reporting. With the Insight Tag, you can track conversions, retarget website visitors, and view Audience Insights on LinkedIn member accounts that visit your website.

chunks.title: LinkedIn Insight Tag | Marketing Solutions Help
chunks.heading: LinkedIn Insight Tag | Marketing Solutions Help > Here's a tip
chunks.text: For the best results, we recommend installing only one Insight Tag per website. If you have multiple ad accounts, you can share an Insight Tag across accounts so that each ad account is able to receive data from the same tag on your site.

chunks.title: LinkedIn Insight Tag | Marketing Solutions Help
chunks.heading: LinkedIn Insight Tag | Marketing Solutions Help > Features available with the Insight Tag
chunks.text:
With the Insight Tag installed on your website or through a tag management system, you can use the below features:

- Conversion Tracking - Create conversions to track when a LinkedIn member account visits a page or takes an action on your website after viewing or clicking your ads.
- Website audiences - Create and build website audiences to retarget LinkedIn member accounts that visit your site.
- Website Actions - When the Insight Tag is installed on your website, you can build conversions and website retargeting audiences based on Website Actions, without requiring additional setup or code. Website Actions automatically collects and tags all the actions potential buyers perform on your website. Learn more about Website Actions, including the button layout and engagement data involved.

When the Insight Tag is installed on your website, you can build conversions and website retargeting audiences based on Website Actions, without requiring additional setup or code. Website Actions automatically collects and tags all the actions potential buyers perform on your website.

chunks.title: LinkedIn Insight Tag | Marketing Solutions Help
chunks.heading: LinkedIn Insight Tag | Marketing Solutions Help > How the Insight Tag works
chunks.text:
When you install the Insight Tag on your site, the tag creates cookies and a first-party pseudonymous identifier called a LinkedIn Ads ID on visitors' web browsers when they visit your website.

- Cookies enable the collection of data regarding member accounts’ visits to your website.
- The LinkedIn Ads ID (li_adsid) is a first-party identifier generated by the Insight Tag to help support conversion tracking as an additional signal on top of cookies. It is only applicable to website traffic from outside the EU, EEA, Quebec, and UK territories.

Each Insight Tag has a unique partner ID that matches the data received from an Insight Tag with an ad account. The partner ID is generated when you create an Insight Tag on your ad account.

chunks.title: LinkedIn Insight Tag | Marketing Solutions Help
chunks.heading: LinkedIn Insight Tag | Marketing Solutions Help > How the Insight Tag works > Here's a tip
chunks.text: We recommend enabling first-party cookies for your Insight Tag to more accurately measure conversions and build website audiences. Many browsers block the creation of third-party cookies by default, which can cause conversion data loss.

chunks.title: LinkedIn Insight Tag | Marketing Solutions Help
chunks.heading: LinkedIn Insight Tag | Marketing Solutions Help > Insight Tag and Microsoft’s UET tag
chunks.text:
Please note, LinkedIn also receives data from Microsoft’s UET tag, which is similar to the Insight Tag and further improves conversion tracking.

- The UET tag helps measure visits to your website. When available, we use this data to capture more website conversions and improve campaign optimization. Please note, data from countries in the European Economic Area (EEA) and Switzerland (Designated Countries) and restricted countries (https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/exporting/faq) is excluded from the information provided by the UET tag. Learn more about the UET tag on the Microsoft website.

- When you use both the Insight Tag and UET tag, conversions are counted using LinkedIn’s existing attribution rules. If the same action is detected by multiple tracking sources, it is only counted once. Learn more about deduplication for conversion tracking.

chunks.title: LinkedIn Insight Tag | Marketing Solutions Help
chunks.heading: LinkedIn Insight Tag | Marketing Solutions Help > Insight Tag and Microsoft’s UET tag
chunks.text:
- We use UET data to help calculate your conversion metrics, so you might see a difference in your conversion data. Keep in mind, the Insight Tag will be the primary data source, with the UET tag providing additional information where available. If you disconnect the UET tag, you could see decreased attributed conversions, depending on where each tag is setup on your website.

Keep in mind, you can disconnect the UET tag in Campaign Manager at any time.

chunks.title: LinkedIn Insight Tag | Marketing Solutions Help
chunks.heading: LinkedIn Insight Tag | Marketing Solutions Help > Preparing for the Insight Tag
chunks.text:
LinkedIn provides services that are meant to be used in a legally compliant manner. You are responsible for ensuring you’ve obtained any necessary permissions or consents from your users before sharing any data with a third-party, including with LinkedIn. LinkedIn is unable to provide legal guidance or recommendations to customers.

We recommend you engage your internal stakeholders, such as your legal counsel, early in the process and share the following resources related to how data shared via Insight Tag will be used:

- LinkedIn's Data Processing Agreement
- LinkedIn Independent Controller Addendum
- LinkedIn’s Ads Agreement

chunks.title: LinkedIn Insight Tag | Marketing Solutions Help
chunks.heading: LinkedIn Insight Tag | Marketing Solutions Help > Insight Tag data privacy > Important to know
chunks.text:
Consistent with our terms, the Insight Tag should not be installed on web pages that collect or contain Sensitive Data. This can include pages offering specific health-related or financial services or products to consumers.

For example, depending on the content of the pages, the Insight Tag may be included on a generic homepage for a pharmacy or a bank, or business-to-business pages directed only to organizations and financial or healthcare professionals, but should not be included on consumer pages for certain types of medications or pages where users manage their financial accounts and transactions or medical appointments, since it could lead to the inadvertent collection and sharing of sensitive information regarding the health or finances of individuals who visited that page.

This does not constitute legal advice. Please consult with your webmaster and legal counsel to determine which pages may or may not collect sensitive data.

When using the Insight Tag, keep in mind the following privacy measures:

chunks.title: LinkedIn Insight Tag | Marketing Solutions Help
chunks.heading: LinkedIn Insight Tag | Marketing Solutions Help > Insight Tag data privacy > Important to know
chunks.text:
When using the Insight Tag, keep in mind the following privacy measures:

- Pseudonymization - Information that directly identifies an individual member is removed from data within seven days in order to make the data pseudonymous.
- Data retention - Remaining pseudonymized data is deleted within 180 days.
- Enhanced matching - If you enable enhanced matching, you can also send email addresses associated with the respective visits. Those email addresses are hashed on the website before being sent to LinkedIn, to protect members’ privacy – we only match information we already have, the rest remains unreadable. Learn more about enhanced matching for your website.
- Data storage - Data is stored in LinkedIn’s servers in the U.S. Please note that LinkedIn complies with the EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework, which ensures an adequate level of protection for personal data transferred from the EU/EEA. Learn more about EU/EEA, UK, and Swiss data transfers.
- Data processing - No subcontractors or sub-processors are involved.
- Member transparency and controls - LinkedIn members can access their ad settings at any time to control how their data may be used for ads, including data that is shared by a customer via the Insight Tag. Members also have the ability to have their data deleted, among other rights, as covered in Section 4 of our Privacy Policy.

Conversions are actions a potential or existing customer takes that are valuable to your business. When you associate conversions with your LinkedIn ad sets, you can measure the impact of your ad campaign’s effectiveness and your return on ad spend (ROAS) on LinkedIn.

You can create and add conversions to your LinkedIn ad sets on the Conversion Tracking page in Campaign Manager or while you’re building your ad set.

chunks.heading: Get started with LinkedIn Conversion Tracking | Marketing Solutions Help > Choose and set up your conversion data source
chunks.text:
Your conversions can be created from four different data sources:

- Conversions API
- Website-based data sources: LinkedIn Insight Tag and Microsoft UET tag
- CRM partner (connected through CRM Sync)
- CSV file upload

LinkedIn also receives data from Microsoft’s UET tag, which is similar to the Insight Tag and further improves conversion tracking. Keep in mind:

- Data from countries in the European Economic Area (EEA) and Switzerland (Designated Countries) and restricted countries (https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/exporting/faq) is excluded from the information provided by the UET tag. Learn more about the UET tag on the Microsoft website. You can also disconnect the UET tag in Campaign Manager at any time.

- When you use both the Insight Tag and UET tag, conversions are counted using LinkedIn’s existing attribution rules. If the same action is detected by multiple tracking sources, it is only counted once. Learn more about deduplication for conversion tracking.

chunks.text: - We use UET data to help calculate your conversion metrics, so you might see a difference in your conversion data. chunks.text:
Before you set up Insight Tag conversions, decide the conversion tracking method you’d like to use:

Conversion Tracking method | Insight Tag required | Description

Website Actions | Required | Website Actions automatically collects and tags all the actions potential buyers perform on your website, like button clicks, page visits, or form submissions, without requiring additional setup or coding.

Manual conversions setup: Page load (sitewide tracking) | Required | Page load conversions are counted when LinkedIn member accounts visit pages on your website. Define which page conversions are counted from by setting URL parameters.

Manual conversions setup: Event specific | Required | Event-specific conversions are counted when LinkedIn member accounts take an action on your website. Add an event-specific code to a link or button on your website to define which actions conversions are counted for.

chunks.title: Set up Conversion Tracking for Insight Tag conversions | Marketing Solutions Help

chunks.text:
Manual conversions setup: Image pixel | Not required (image pixel) | Image pixel (event-specific tracking) conversions are counted when LinkedIn member accounts take an action on your website. You'll need to install an event-specific image pixel that loads when the conversion action is taken.

Tag manager | Required | Choose this option if you’re using a tag manager to implement your Insight Tag and track conversions. The LinkedIn Insight Tag is currently supported by Google, Adobe, Tealium, Ensighten, and Floodlight.

Conversions based on the Insight Tag, such as page load tracking or event tracking, enable both first- and third-party cookies. Event-specific image pixel conversions are less accurate, since they only enable third-party cookies, and you can't use enhanced conversion tracking with image pixel.

- If you add a new action to your website, such as a new button or a new page, it’ll be automatically captured and added to your Website Actions list. New Website Actions are reflected in Campaign Manager within 48 hours after you add them to your website.

chunks.title: Understanding Website Actions | Marketing Solutions Help
chunks.heading: Understanding Website Actions | Marketing Solutions Help > Website Actions data information
chunks.text:
Website Actions are built on LinkedIn’s Insight Tag. The LinkedIn Insight Tag enables the collection of data regarding members’ visits to your website, including the URL, referrer, IP address, device and browser characteristics (User Agent), and timestamp. The IP addresses are truncated or hashed (when used for reaching members across devices), and members’ direct identifiers are removed within seven days in order to make the data pseudonymous. This remaining pseudonymized data is then deleted within 180 days.

If you choose to use Website Actions, some additional, limited data will be collected to enable classification of events:

HTML DOM elements - For example, button text and page name.

-

Button action - Whether someone clicked or viewed a button.

-

Session-unique user hash - Used to count unique actions on your site.

chunks.title: Deduplication for Conversion Tracking | Marketing Solutions Help
chunks.heading: Deduplication for Conversion Tracking | Marketing Solutions Help
chunks.text: When setting up your conversion tracking methods, we recommend that you send events through both a website tag (like the LinkedIn Insight Tag, Microsoft UET tag, or the image pixel) and Conversions API for increased reliability and a more complete view of the customer journey. The website tag shares events from a browser and Conversions API shares events from your server.

chunks.title: Deduplication for Conversion Tracking | Marketing Solutions Help
chunks.heading: Deduplication for Conversion Tracking | Marketing Solutions Help > Deduplication overview
chunks.text:
Using multiple methods to share events is known as a redundant setup. It’s important to keep in mind, if you’re using a redundant setup, we might receive the same events from both the browser and the server. To prevent counting the same events more than once, you’ll need to set up deduplication.

Deduplication allows us to identify the same events being passed using multiple methods, discard the duplicate (redundant) event, and only count the conversion once.

chunks.title: Deduplication for Conversion Tracking | Marketing Solutions Help
chunks.heading: Deduplication for Conversion Tracking | Marketing Solutions Help > How deduplication works
chunks.text:
For any conversion that you send through multiple methods, you must create a conversion rule for each data source (browser and server). After you create a conversion rule, you can implement a logic to pick up the eventId from the browser and send it with the corresponding event from your server.

For example, if we receive an Insight Tag event and a Conversions API event from the same account with the same eventId, we discard the Conversions API event and only count the Insight Tag event in campaign reporting.

Please note, if you’re using multiple website tag methods (for example, both the Insight Tag and the UET tag), we’ll deduplicate if the same conversion event happens at the same time. For example, if someone visits a sign-up page and triggers both the Insight Tag and the UET tag, the conversion event will only be counted once.

chunks.title: Deduplication for Conversion Tracking | Marketing Solutions Help
chunks.heading: Deduplication for Conversion Tracking | Marketing Solutions Help > Set up deduplication
chunks.text: To set up deduplication, please review our Deduplication documentation in the Microsoft Help Center. You can set up deduplication manually or through your Tag Manager. After you set up deduplication, check that both the Conversions API event and the Insight Tag event are showing in Campaign Manager. To review, go to your Conversion Tracking page, and make sure Conversions is selected at the top.

chunks.title: Deduplication for Conversion Tracking | Marketing Solutions Help
chunks.heading: Deduplication for Conversion Tracking | Marketing Solutions Help > Set up deduplication > Here's a tip
chunks.text:
Because we deduct redundant events from the Conversions API conversion count, the Insight Tag event will typically have a higher count if deduplication is working correctly.

chunks.title: Using modeled conversions to measure conversions for LinkedIn Ads | Marketing Solutions Help
chunks.heading: Using modeled conversions to measure conversions for LinkedIn Ads | Marketing Solutions Help
chunks.text:
We generally measure conversions for each LinkedIn member who takes an action on your ad. However, to protect member privacy and evolve with industry-wide privacy changes, we are evolving the way we measure conversions.

To capture as many conversions as possible, we increasingly use machine learning to estimate conversions in place of using third-party individual-level data. We combine member engagement data with technologies such as machine learning to predict conversions in instances where a conversion is no longer observable due to industry-wide privacy change or member setting selections. In instances where first-party individual-level data is available, we measure conversions deterministically. Deterministic means we can make an exact match between a conversion and an ad campaign at the member-level.

Modeled conversions are included in your reporting, and are reported in the same dimensions and metrics as other conversions.

chunks.heading: LinkedIn Conversions API | Marketing Solutions Help
chunks.text:
With Conversions API, you can connect both your online and offline data to LinkedIn so you can see how your campaigns influenced actions taken on your website, sales completed over the phone, or leads collected in-person at an event.

Using Conversions API allows you to:

- Send marketing data directly from your server to LinkedIn to measure the performance of your LinkedIn campaigns using LinkedIn’s Conversions API.
- Improve full-funnel measurement by connecting online and offline conversions to LinkedIn to measure performance across your entire customer journey.
- Power your ad sets with multiple types of conversion data to drive more of the actions you care about.
- Strengthen performance and privacy by driving a more efficient Cost Per Action with a reliable and secure data connection that doesn’t rely on cookie-based tracking.
- Increase data control by deciding how you share data with LinkedIn.

Learn more about deduplication in the Microsoft Help Center.

chunks.title: LinkedIn Conversions API | Marketing Solutions Help
chunks.heading: LinkedIn Conversions API | Marketing Solutions Help > When to use Conversions API
chunks.text:
Conversions API is a good choice to use to:

- Strengthen your existing conversion tracking. You can use Conversions API and the Insight Tag together to measure online and offline events across your customer journey.
- You’d like to optimize your ad set toward qualified leads. To use qualified leads as the optimization goal for your ad set, we recommend setting up Conversions API first. Learn more about the qualified leads optimization goal.
- Send data to LinkedIn continuously and automatically, as well as when you have larger volumes of conversions that need to be sent at high frequency. With a CSV document, you must manually upload your data, which can result in older information and requires more resources.

- Data terms and usage - Conversions API is covered by LinkedIn’s Data Processing Agreement. Data shared via Conversions API will be used in accordance with Section 13 of LinkedIn's Ads Agreement.
- Pseudonymization - Email addresses are hashed using SHA-256.
- Data retention - Data is deleted after 180 days. The only data that persists is the aggregate conversion reporting in Campaign Manager. In addition, LinkedIn can facilitate deletion requests within 180 days from customers where received.
- Data storage - Data is stored in LinkedIn’s servers in the U.S. Please note that LinkedIn complies with the EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework, which ensures an adequate level of protection for personal data transferred from the EU/EEA. Learn more about EU/EEA, UK, and Swiss data transfers.
- Data processing - All data processing is done by LinkedIn on LinkedIn’s servers in the U.S. No subcontractors or sub-processors are involved.
- Member transparency and controls - LinkedIn members can access their ad settings at any time to control how their data, including data that is shared by a marketer via Conversions API, may be used for ads. Members also have the ability to have their data deleted, among other rights, as covered in Section 4 of our Privacy Policy.

chunks.text: Once you’ve set up Conversions API (CAPI) in Campaign Manager, we recommend the following best practices to help optimize your connection and provide a more robust measurement solution.

chunks.title: Conversions API setup in Campaign Manager best practices | Marketing Solutions Help
chunks.heading: Conversions API setup in Campaign Manager best practices | Marketing Solutions Help > Confirm that you’re sending events in real time
chunks.text:
When you create conversions based on your CAPI integration, you can send data in real time to LinkedIn. Real-time data helps ensure that the data can be attributed and used while it is relevant.

Learn how to review your CAPI setup to ensure that we’re receiving data in real time and that your conversions are active and ready to use.

chunks.title: Conversions API setup in Campaign Manager best practices | Marketing Solutions Help
chunks.heading: Conversions API setup in Campaign Manager best practices | Marketing Solutions Help > Send a same (static) or dynamic conversion value with your conversions
chunks.text:
When you’re creating your conversion, we recommend that you assign a conversion value. With a conversion value, you can learn more about your return on investment (ROI), instead of only seeing the number of conversions that happened.

Learn about the different types of conversion values (same and dynamic).

chunks.title: Conversions API setup in Campaign Manager best practices | Marketing Solutions Help
chunks.heading: Conversions API setup in Campaign Manager best practices | Marketing Solutions Help > Choose the right conversion window for your conversion
chunks.text:
After setting a value for your conversion, you’ll also need to set up a conversion window (lookback window). You’ll typically want a longer conversion window to increase your chances of attributing a tracked conversion.

For most conversions, we recommend a 90-day click, 90-day view window, which is the default in Campaign Manager.

With CAPI, you can also manually set your conversion window timeframe to 1, 7, 30, or 90 days. Or, if you have a long sales cycle or infrequent conversions, you can choose either the 180- or 365-day conversion window for some conversion categories: Submit Application, Purchase, Add to Cart, Qualified Lead, Marketing Qualified Lead, Sales Qualified Lead, and Lead.

Learn more about LinkedIn’s conversion windows.

chunks.title: Conversions API setup in Campaign Manager best practices | Marketing Solutions Help
chunks.heading: Conversions API setup in Campaign Manager best practices | Marketing Solutions Help > Choose the right attribution model for your marketing goals
chunks.text:
When setting up your conversions, you can select how each ad interaction is credited for a conversion across multiple ad sets. For most conversion types, we use the last-touch attribution model. This means that if a member converts multiple times within the conversion window, we'll count it as a single conversion. The conversion will be attributed to the most recent ad click or view from that member.

You’ll need to choose if the attribution model is set for each ad set or a single ad set.

- Each ad set - Gives credit to all ad sets that had an ad interaction within that window. We recommend this model for measuring across the full funnel, since it credits all ad sets the user interacted with.
- Last ad set - Gives conversion credit once, which allows you to report on the impact of your LinkedIn investment as a whole.

Learn more about LinkedIn’s conversion attribution model.

chunks.heading: Conversions API setup in Campaign Manager best practices | Marketing Solutions Help > Associate your conversions to multiple ad sets
chunks.text:
When you associate your conversions to as many applicable ad sets as possible, it helps maximize chances of attributing a conversion. When you’re creating your conversion, we’ll automatically associate ad sets to your conversion. You have the option to review, add, and remove ad sets as needed.

Learn more about auto-selected ad sets when creating your conversion in Campaign Manager.

chunks.title: Troubleshoot Conversions API signal quality | Marketing Solutions Help
chunks.heading: Troubleshoot Conversions API signal quality | Marketing Solutions Help
chunks.text:
When Conversions API (CAPI) events are streamed to LinkedIn, we evaluate the signal quality, which is the effectiveness of matching the event to a LinkedIn profile. We recommend that you monitor your signal quality, since it can help increase conversions and improve your cost per result.

If you see Low Match Rate below Active for your conversion, this means that the information streamed to LinkedIn has a low likelihood of successful event-to-profile matching. Keep in mind, this is only applicable for conversions based on Direct API integration.

chunks.title: Troubleshoot Conversions API signal quality | Marketing Solutions Help
chunks.heading: Troubleshoot Conversions API signal quality | Marketing Solutions Help > Here's a tip
chunks.text:
To find the signal quality for your Conversions API event, go to the Conversion Tracking page in Campaign Manager.

If your signal quality is low, please review the following sections below to help troubleshoot any issues:

- Include new identifiers supported by Conversions API (CAPI)
- Provide more matching parameters
- Maintain consistent event volume
- Send the highest impact identifiers for each event
- Use both Conversions API and the LinkedIn Insight Tag with enhanced conversion tracking

chunks.title: Troubleshoot Conversions API signal quality | Marketing Solutions Help
chunks.heading: Troubleshoot Conversions API signal quality | Marketing Solutions Help > Include new identifiers supported by Conversions API (CAPI)
chunks.text:
As of May 2026, you can include two new matching identifiers with your CAPI events: IP address (IPv4) and Google Advertising ID (GAID) as complementary signals.

- IP address (IPv4) - Support matching for upper-funnel events, such as page views and content views.
- GAID - Helps improve match quality for mobile app and cross-device activity.

chunks.title: Troubleshoot Conversions API signal quality | Marketing Solutions Help
chunks.heading: Troubleshoot Conversions API signal quality | Marketing Solutions Help > Provide more matching parameters
chunks.text:
To improve the signal quality and performance for Conversions API (CAPI) integrations, we recommend that you add information to as many matching parameters as possible. This helps us better optimize your campaigns and reporting.

Recommendation | Additional information

Use user IDs whenever possible to help increase match rates. | Only matched events can be used for attribution and optimization. Review the table below for more information on our supported IDs for both direct and partner integrations.

Provide information for as many parameters as possible to help improve signal quality. | For Direct API integrations, you can find a full list of IDs in our Conversions API developer documentation.

For partner integrations, you can set up the parameters when connecting to your partner. Use your partner’s instructions to pass as many matching parameters as possible.

chunks.title: Troubleshoot Conversions API signal quality | Marketing Solutions Help
chunks.heading: Troubleshoot Conversions API signal quality | Marketing Solutions Help > Maintain consistent event volume
chunks.text:
Send your events consistently over time to help ensure reliable measurement and optimization. Sudden drops in event volume can indicate tracking issues and inconsistent event delivery can reduce optimization effectiveness.

To help make sure you’re maintaining consistent event volume, we recommend that you:

- Verify that events are firing across all relevant user actions.
- Review your CAPI setup regularly to make sure it’s stable and sending events continuously.

chunks.title: Troubleshoot Conversions API signal quality | Marketing Solutions Help
chunks.heading: Troubleshoot Conversions API signal quality | Marketing Solutions Help > Send the highest impact identifiers for each event
chunks.text:
Because conversion match rates depend on the identifiers included in each event, make sure that you’re sending the most impactful identifiers specific to the event.

A low match rate can indicate missing or insufficient identifiers. It can also show that you’re not sending the best identifiers for that event, since some event types benefit from different identifier strategies.

To help ensure that you’re sending the highest impact identifiers for your event, we recommend that you:

- Include primary identifies whenever possible. For example, include email for lead events.
- Add the most relevant secondary identifiers, such as including IP address for page view events.
- Review your identifiers and make sure they align to your event type and the available data.

chunks.title: Troubleshoot Conversions API signal quality | Marketing Solutions Help
chunks.heading: Troubleshoot Conversions API signal quality | Marketing Solutions Help > Use both Conversions API (CAPI) and the LinkedIn Insight Tag with enhanced conversion tracking
chunks.text:
You can also use both CAPI and the LinkedIn Insight Tag with enhanced conversion tracking to get the most complete view of the customer journey.

A few considerations to keep in mind when you use both CAPI and Insight Tag:

- When you use both the Insight Tag and CAPI, if we identify an event has been sent through both, we can deduplicate it and only count it once.
- When you send a conversion through both Insight Tag and CAPI, you need to create a conversion rule for each data source (browser and server).

chunks.title: Troubleshoot Conversions API signal quality | Marketing Solutions Help
chunks.heading: Troubleshoot Conversions API signal quality | Marketing Solutions Help > Use both Conversions API (CAPI) and the LinkedIn Insight Tag with enhanced conversion tracking > Here's a tip
chunks.text:
Purchase and Add to Cart conversions are always counted individually, even if those actions were completed by the same member within the lookback window.

We recommend that enhanced conversion tracking is enabled on your Insight Tag. Enhanced conversion tracking allows you to use first-party cookies to better capture website audiences and conversions.

- When you're using enhanced conversion tracking, LinkedIn’s first-party Click ID, known as li_fat_id or LINKEDIN_FIRST_PARTY _ADS_TRACKING_UUID, will be added to the end of landing page URLs to allow for first-party cookie tracking.
- You don’t have to install the Insight Tag to use enhanced conversion tracking, but you must create it in Campaign Manager. However, when you don’t install the Insight Tag on your website, Insight Tag conversion tracking and view-through conversions aren't available. Learn how to check if enhanced conversion tracking is enabled.

The following table describes how the Insight Tag and enhanced conversion tracking works for your conversion tracking.

Insight Tag | Enhanced tracking | How it works | Types of conversion tracking supported by enhanced tracking | Considerations

Added to website | Enabled | Every time a user clicks on an ad and is redirected to a landing page, the click ID will be added to the landing page URL and the cookie store.

The cookie will persist for 30 days from the most recent click that redirected to the landing page.

chunks.heading: Troubleshoot Conversions API signal quality | Marketing Solutions Help > Use both Conversions API (CAPI) and the LinkedIn Insight Tag with enhanced conversion tracking > Important to know
chunks.text:
Consistent with our terms, the Insight Tag should not be installed on web pages that collect or contain Sensitive Data. This can include pages offering specific health-related or financial services or products to consumers.

For example, depending on the content of the pages, the Insight Tag may be included on a generic homepage for a pharmacy or a bank, or business-to-business pages directed only to organizations and financial or healthcare professionals, but should not be included on consumer pages for certain types of medications or pages where users manage their financial accounts and transactions or medical appointments, since it could lead to the inadvertent collection and sharing of sensitive information regarding the health or finances of individuals who visited that page.

This does not constitute legal advice. Please consult with your webmaster and legal counsel to determine which pages may or may not collect sensitive data.

chunks.text:
You must have a GTM account with a web container installed on your website. If this is your first time using GTM, you’ll need to set up your account and create a web container. After your web container is set up:

- Configure a trigger in the web container that fires the Google Analytics 4 (GA4) event you want to track as a conversion.
- Save the GA4 measurement ID. You may be asked to provide it during conversion setup in Campaign Manager. Learn how to find your GA4 measurement ID in GTM in the Google Help Center.

Then, you’ll need a server container. We recommend you set up your server container when you're creating your conversion in Campaign Manager through Stape.

chunks.heading: Create conversions with Conversions API and Google Tag Manager | Marketing Solutions Help > Before you create your conversion > Option 1 (recommended): Set up server-side tracking with Stape when creating your conversion in Campaign Manager
chunks.text:
Instead of manually setting up your server in GTM, we recommend you choose to set up server-side tracking with Stape when creating your conversion in Campaign Manager. Stape will automatically create and host your server-side GTM container, which saves you set up time and helps you create your conversions faster and more seamlessly within Campaign Manager, without any additional code required.

Please note, eligible advertisers can create and host one Stape server-side Google Tag Manager container per eligible LinkedIn ad account at no additional cost when the container is created through the Stape setup flow embedded in LinkedIn Campaign Manager. Learn more about the terms and eligibility for using Stape.

chunks.title: Create conversions with Conversions API and Google Tag Manager | Marketing Solutions Help
chunks.heading: Create conversions with Conversions API and Google Tag Manager | Marketing Solutions Help > Before you create your conversion > Option 2: Manually set up server-side tracking in Google Tag Manager
chunks.text:
You can also manually set up a server container in Google Tag Manager (GTM). For this option, you’ll need to:

- Configure a GTM server container and create a GA4 client to receive events from your web container. Review Google’s Server-side tagging and Custom tag template documentation before setting up your container.

- Save the Server container URL, which you’ll need during conversion setup.

Begin creating your conversion in Campaign Manager. Choose Conversions API as your data source and create your conversion rule.

chunks.title: Create conversions with Conversions API and Google Tag Manager | Marketing Solutions Help
chunks.heading: Create conversions with Conversions API and Google Tag Manager | Marketing Solutions Help > Set up the data from Google Tag Manager to send to Campaign Manager
chunks.text:
Follow the steps below to set up your connection with Google Tag Manager.

Keep in mind, Google Tag Manager will automatically collect user data matching identifiers for conversion tracking. They’re used to improve the quality of events streamed to LinkedIn. The following fields are automatically collected:

- Email
- Name
- Country code
- li_fat_id
- ip_address

Learn more about Google Tag Manager automatic collection in the Google Help Center, and the types of streaming conversion events on the Microsoft Learn site.

-

In the Google Tag Manager account section, click the Select the account dropdown menu and select your account name.

-

In the Containers section, click the dropdown menus to select:

- An existing web container
- A workspace for the web container

-

In the Server-side tracking section, select how you’d like to set up your container:

- Automatic setup with Stape (recommended) - Select the Set up now button and follow the on-screen instructions to connect your account.
- Manual setup in Google Tag Manager - Add your existing server container and workspace.

chunks.title: Create conversions with Conversions API and Google Tag Manager | Marketing Solutions Help
chunks.heading: Create conversions with Conversions API and Google Tag Manager | Marketing Solutions Help > Set up the data from Google Tag Manager to send to Campaign Manager > Here's a tip
chunks.text:

-

In the Tags section, select how you’d like to set up your server:

- If you used Stape to create your server container, your tag will automatically be created, and no action is required.
- Automatic setup with Stape (Recommended) - If you set up your own server container but would like to use Stape for your tagging server, select the Set up now button and follow the on-screen instructions to connect your account.
- Manual setup in Google Tag Manager - Add your Google Analytics 4 (GA4) measurement ID, Tagging server URL, and select the web GA4 event trigger from the Select existing trigger dropdown menu.

-

In the Token section, paste your LinkedIn API access token. If you don’t have a token, you can generate one by clicking the Generate token button.

-

Click Next step.

Once published, your conversions will begin sending to LinkedIn. It might take a few hours before you see the conversion data appear in Campaign Manager.

We recommend you review the following best practices when creating a CSV conversion.

Topic | Best practice

Choose the right conversion window for your conversions | For most conversions, choose a longer conversion window to help increase your chances of attributing a tracked conversion. We typically recommend a 90-day click, 90-day view window, which is the default in Campaign Manager.

For long sales cycles or infrequent conversions, you can choose either the 180- or 365-day conversion window for the following conversion events: Submit Application, Purchase, Add to Cart, Qualified Lead, Marketing Qualified Lead, Sales Qualified Lead, and Lead.

Maximize conversions in your ad sets | You generally want to associate your conversions to as many applicable ad sets as possible to maximize chances of attributing a conversion.

chunks.heading: LinkedIn conversion attribution model | Marketing Solutions Help
chunks.text:
When setting up your conversions, you can select how each ad interaction is credited for a conversion across multiple ad sets. For most conversion types, we use the last-touch attribution model. This means, if a member converts multiple times within the conversion window, we'll count it as a single conversion. The conversion will be attributed to the most recent ad click or view from that member.

The attribution model can be set to each ad set or a single ad set.

- Last touch - Each ad set - For a conversion action associated with multiple ad sets, every ad set that has had an interaction in the conversion window will get credited with a conversion.
- Last touch - Last ad set - For a conversion action associated with an ad set, the most recent ad set that has had an ad interaction in the conversion window will get credited with a conversion.

chunks.title: LinkedIn conversion window | Marketing Solutions Help
chunks.heading: LinkedIn conversion window | Marketing Solutions Help
chunks.text:
A conversion window, also known as a lookback window, is the timeframe for when conversions are attributed to a LinkedIn ad. Advertisers can customize their conversion windows based on their reporting preferences.

LinkedIn records conversions within the selected conversion window in two ways:

- Views - Also known as a view-through conversion, this records when a member sees a LinkedIn Ad.
- Clicks - Also known as a post-click conversion, this records when a member clicks on a LinkedIn Ad.

chunks.title: LinkedIn conversion window | Marketing Solutions Help
chunks.heading: LinkedIn conversion window | Marketing Solutions Help > Conversion window timeframes
chunks.text:
When setting up your conversion, you need to select the timeframe for when the conversion can be counted. You typically will want to use a longer conversion window to increase your chances of attributing a tracked conversion.

For most conversions, we recommend a 90-day click, 90-day view window, which is the default in Campaign Manager.

- For all conversions - You can manually set your conversion window timeframe to 1, 7, 30, or 90 days.
- For Conversions API (CAPI) or CSV conversions - If you have a long sales cycle or infrequent conversions and you use CAPI or a CSV file upload, you can also choose either the 180- or 365-day lookback window for some conversion categories: Submit Application, Purchase, Add to Cart, Qualified Lead, Marketing Qualified Lead, Sales Qualified Lead, and Lead.

chunks.title: LinkedIn conversion window | Marketing Solutions Help
chunks.heading: LinkedIn conversion window | Marketing Solutions Help > Conversion window timeframes > Important to know
chunks.text: As of April 2025, the click attribution window for event registration conversions increased from 7 to 30 days, and the view attribution window increased from 1 to 30 days. As a result, you may see an increase in event registrations and return on investment (ROI).

chunks.title: LinkedIn conversion window | Marketing Solutions Help
chunks.heading: LinkedIn conversion window | Marketing Solutions Help > How conversions are counted within the conversion window
chunks.text:
For most conversion types, we use the last-touch attribution model. If a member converts multiple times within the conversion window, we'll count it as a single conversion. The conversion will then be attributed to the most recent ad click or view from that member.

However, when you select Purchase or Add to Cart as the conversion type, multiple conversion events may be reported by one member. If one member converts multiple times within the conversion window, we’ll count each of the conversion events. Learn more about our conversion attribution model.

chunks.heading: LinkedIn conversion window | Marketing Solutions Help > How conversions are counted within the conversion window > Important to know
chunks.text:

chunks.heading: LinkedIn Conversion Tracking reporting and metrics | Marketing Solutions Help > Here's a tip
chunks.text:
For CSV conversions, it typically takes between 24 and 48 hours for data to be available for reporting. In some instances, it can take up to one week. For Conversions API, the time it takes for the data to be available depends on the type of conversion. Check the status based on the typical frequency of the conversion event.

Conversion Tracking metrics include:

Metric | Definition

Conversions | Total number of times users took a desired action, such as a download or sign-up, after clicking on or seeing your ad.

When conversions can’t be attributed to individual users, we may use modeled conversions to measure conversions in place of using individual-level data.

Click Conversions | The number of clicks on your ads that led to a conversion.

View Conversions | The number of views of your ads that led to a conversion.

For example, sometimes a user will view your ad, visit your website later, and then convert. Even though this user might not have clicked the ad, LinkedIn will attribute these types of conversions to your ad set if the user converts within the timeframe you chose when setting up your conversion.

chunks.heading: LinkedIn Conversion Tracking reporting and metrics | Marketing Solutions Help > Here's a tip

Cost Per Conversion | The average amount you spent on each conversion (total spent divided by conversions).

Total Conversion Value | The total value generated by your conversions (value per conversion multiplied by conversions). This value can be defined when creating conversion actions, which is how much you consider each conversion is worth to you.

Return on Ad Spend | The revenue generated for ad spend (total conversion value divided by amount spent).

chunks.title: Attribution Model metrics for leads and conversions in Campaign Manager | Marketing Solutions Help
chunks.heading: Attribution Model metrics for leads and conversions in Campaign Manager | Marketing Solutions Help > Considerations for Attribution Model metrics
chunks.text:
When you select Attribution Model as your view, keep in mind the following considerations.

Consideration | Explanation

Data refresh time in Campaign Manager | Data-driven attribution metrics can take up to 36 hours (on a rare occasion, longer) to appear in Campaign Manager. There can be a discrepancy between the information in Campaign Manager if you check the table before the data-driven attribution leads information has updated.

Leads information updates in real time.

Metric availability | You can view the metrics at the campaign, ad set, and ad level.

Difference between Leads and Leads (data-driven attribution) when using filtering | The sum of the Leads column (shown at the top of the column) might be different than the sum of the Leads (data-driven attribution) column when you filter by specific campaigns, ad sets, or ads.

This is because the Leads column only reports leads directly submitted to that ad set, whereas the Leads (data-driven attribution) column includes each ad set's contribution for leads submitted through any ad set in your account.

chunks.title: Attribution Model metrics for leads and conversions in Campaign Manager | Marketing Solutions Help
chunks.heading: Attribution Model metrics for leads and conversions in Campaign Manager | Marketing Solutions Help > Considerations for Attribution Model metrics
chunks.text:

To minimize discrepancies, we recommend that you clear all filters from your campaign dashboard and choose a date range that ends at least two days before the current date, since data can take up to 36 hours to update.

chunks.title: Compare Campaign Manager conversions with third-party reporting | Marketing Solutions Help
chunks.heading: Compare Campaign Manager conversions with third-party reporting | Marketing Solutions Help
chunks.text:
The LinkedIn Insight Tag records conversions based on the rules you implement when setting up your conversion tracking. However, the conversion data recorded may not match what you see on other third-party reporting platforms (for example, Google Analytics). Below are the most common reasons for reporting discrepancies.

When creating a conversion, you must add it to one or more ad sets to enable conversion tracking. If your ad set isn't recording conversions, it's an indication that you may not have added a conversion to that ad set.

Learn how to set up an Insight Tag conversions.

chunks.title: Compare Campaign Manager conversions with third-party reporting | Marketing Solutions Help
chunks.heading: Compare Campaign Manager conversions with third-party reporting | Marketing Solutions Help > Here's a tip
chunks.text:
You can view the exact ad sets associated with a conversion on your Conversion Tracking page in Campaign Manager. On that page, find your conversion, then click the number in the Ad sets selected column and select Edit to see all.

To check if you've previously added a conversion to an ad set:

-

Go to your ad account in Campaign Manager.

-

Click Advertise on the left menu.

-

Select the Ad sets tab at the top, then find your ad set.

-

Move your cursor over the ad set name, then click Edit.

-

Scroll to the Conversion tracking (optional) section to see all conversions attached to the ad set and add more if necessary.

Campaign Manager gathers conversion data through a third-party cookie system, whereas some third-party reporting platforms like Google Analytics are a first-party cookie system.

Any browser that is set to not accept third-party cookies won't be tracked by Campaign Manager. For example, Safari and Apple Mobile Devices have default settings to block third-party cookies. Browsers opened through the LinkedIn app are able to accept and collect data on third-party cookies.

chunks.title: Compare Campaign Manager conversions with third-party reporting | Marketing Solutions Help
chunks.heading: Compare Campaign Manager conversions with third-party reporting | Marketing Solutions Help > Here's a tip
chunks.text:
The LinkedIn Insight tag may not have been installed on all web pages where the third-party tag is present. If you're using Google Analytics, you can use the All Pages report to see all the pages where your Google Analytics tag is firing.

If required, you may use a third-party browser plug-in tool (such as Ghostery), which allows you to quickly identify what tags are firing on a specific page of your site. Learn more about setting up your LinkedIn Insight Tag.

If your conversion includes multiple URLs, you may not have the same URLs being tracked in both systems. Monitoring that all potential conversion point URLs are included within the conversion, helps keep reporting consistent.

Confirm that the URL being tracked as a conversion point in your third-party system matches the URL listed in Campaign Manager, paying close attention to if the URL includes www or any additional slashes or characters that may not be listed in one of the platforms you're using. Learn more about troubleshooting your conversion tracking.

chunks.title: Compare Campaign Manager conversions with third-party reporting | Marketing Solutions Help
chunks.heading: Compare Campaign Manager conversions with third-party reporting | Marketing Solutions Help > Here's a tip
chunks.text:
Ensure that you properly used the URL match rule formatting function in the action setup page. Incorrect use of these matching rules could result in improper tracking of pages and missing conversions. Learn more about setting up conversion tracking.

Since LinkedIn conversions are only counted if someone reaches a conversion URL and has been served a LinkedIn ad, discrepancies can occur if the landing page doesn't properly tie to the conversion URL. For example, if your conversion URL is a "Thank You" page that a member sees after filling out your website's "Contact Us" form but the landing page you've entered into Campaign Manager doesn't have a way for the user to reach the Contact Us page, it's unlikely that many conversions will be counted.

Additionally, we recommend performing a test conversion to get the full information on what URL you reach after doing so. For example, if your conversion in Campaign Manager includes an exact match of the URL "www.advertiser.com/thankyou" but when performing a test action the URL actually renders as "www.advertiser.com/thankyou123", the URLs wouldn't match and therefore wouldn't be counted as a conversion.

chunks.title: Compare Campaign Manager conversions with third-party reporting | Marketing Solutions Help
chunks.heading: Compare Campaign Manager conversions with third-party reporting | Marketing Solutions Help > Here's a tip
chunks.text:
The lookback window for conversion attributions in Campaign Manager is customizable for both views and clicks to 1, 7, or 30 days. Any variance in lookback windows between this and your third-party reporting can result in discrepancies.

Third-party platforms can have different rules and settings for what is determined to be a duplicate conversion. Below is a list of when Campaign Manager does and doesn't deduplicate conversions, with examples.

-

Conversions between ad sets aren't deduplicated.

Example: Ad Set A and Ad Set B are both associated to Conversion 1. A member account is served Ad Y from Ad Set A and converts, the member account is then served Ad Z from Ad Set B and converts. Both conversions will be counted.

-

Conversions categorized as Purchase or Add to Cart won't be deduplicated.

Example: Ad Set is associated with a conversion with Purchase as the conversion category. When a member account is served Ad A and converts, and then is served Ad B and converts, both conversions will be counted.

chunks.title: Compare Campaign Manager conversions with third-party reporting | Marketing Solutions Help
chunks.heading: Compare Campaign Manager conversions with third-party reporting | Marketing Solutions Help > Here's a tip
chunks.text:
By contrast, if the conversion category isn't Purchase or Add to Cart, multiple conversions from the same member account will be deduped in your analytics for a given action within the same ad set. In other words, for all conversion categories except Purchase and Add to Cart within the same ad set, only one conversion per member account per conversion action will be counted during your lookback window, even if that member account converts multiple times during that period.

-

Conversions with multiple URLs listed within the conversion will be deduplicated between URLs.

Example: Conversion 1 includes yourbusiness.com/thankyou and yourbusiness.com/thankyou1. Ad Set A and Ad Set B are both associated to Conversion 1. A member account is served Ad Y from Ad Set A and converts on yourbusiness.com/thankyou, and then is then served Ad Z from Ad Set B and converts on yourbusiness.com/thankyou1. This will be counted as 1 conversion, with priority given to the post-click conversion.

-

We recommend separating your conversion URLs into separate actions to the extent that each URL represents a unique offer for which you'd like to track conversions distinctly.

chunks.title: Compare Campaign Manager conversions with third-party reporting | Marketing Solutions Help
chunks.heading: Compare Campaign Manager conversions with third-party reporting | Marketing Solutions Help > Here's a tip
chunks.text: Currently LinkedIn does not track any conversions that are the result of viral impressions or clicks within the Campaign Manager tool. This means that if a member account clicks or views a LinkedIn Ad due to another member account liking, commenting, or sharing Sponsored Content and then converts, this won't be tracked in Campaign Manager as it isn't a conversion attributed to a paid click or impression. These viral conversions are available by downloading a report from your reporting dashboard.

chunks.title: Compare Campaign Manager conversions with third-party reporting | Marketing Solutions Help
chunks.heading: Compare Campaign Manager conversions with third-party reporting | Marketing Solutions Help > Important to know
chunks.text:
Consistent with our terms, the Insight Tag should not be installed on web pages that collect or contain Sensitive Data. This can include pages offering specific health-related or financial services or products to consumers.

For example, depending on the content of the pages, the Insight Tag may be included on a generic homepage for a pharmacy or a bank, or business-to-business pages directed only to organizations and financial or healthcare professionals, but should not be included on consumer pages for certain types of medications or pages where users manage their financial accounts and transactions or medical appointments, since it could lead to the inadvertent collection and sharing of sensitive information regarding the health or finances of individuals who visited that page.

This does not constitute legal advice. Please consult with your webmaster and legal counsel to determine which pages may or may not collect sensitive data.

chunks.title: Revenue Attribution Report in Business Manager | Marketing Solutions Help
chunks.heading: Revenue Attribution Report in Business Manager | Marketing Solutions Help
chunks.text: The Revenue Attribution Report in Business Manager attributes your Customer Relationship Management (CRM) data to ad activities on LinkedIn. With the Revenue Attribution Report, you can use deeper data points, such as sales revenue, pipeline generated, and win rates, to show how your marketing investments influence business outcomes.

chunks.title: Revenue Attribution Report in Business Manager | Marketing Solutions Help
chunks.heading: Revenue Attribution Report in Business Manager | Marketing Solutions Help > Important to know
chunks.text:
Currently, you can connect your Salesforce, Dynamics 365, or HubSpot CRM to Business Manager.

With your Revenue Attribution Report, you can:

- Connect marketing efforts to real business outcomes by attributing your CRM data to LinkedIn Ads activities.
- Help justify the business impact of your LinkedIn marketing spend.
- Unlock marketing and sales alignment with a common set of metrics focused on revenue impact and business growth.

In the report, you can view:

- Topline metrics - Show the overall effectiveness of LinkedIn as a marketing channel with metrics like revenue won, return on ad spend, and pipeline amount.
- Funnel metrics - Better understand how LinkedIn marketing drove leads and opportunities with metrics like leads, open opportunities, and closed-won opportunities. Download the exportable opportunity and company report to view which specific opportunities are driving revenue, and see how your LinkedIn campaigns are moving companies through the funnel.
- Conversion metrics - See the overall quality and conversion rate of LinkedIn-driven leads with metrics like lead conversion rate, opportunity win rate, and average days to close.

chunks.title: Revenue Attribution Report in Business Manager | Marketing Solutions Help
chunks.heading: Revenue Attribution Report in Business Manager | Marketing Solutions Help > Attribution models
chunks.text:
Currently, the Revenue Attribution Report offers both impression-based and engagement-based attribution models. Engagements include any social action, click to Landing Page, or click to LinkedIn Page, whether chargeable or free. You can specify how many touch-points are needed within the given lookback window to count as LinkedIn marketing influence.

Attribution can be viewed at the member- or company-level based on your unique goals.
